prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one exceptionally high-fidelity desktop educational website screenshot, landscape 1440x1080 approximately, showing the opening viewport plus next-section preview. A finished functioning website design, no browser/device frame.
STRUCTURE in order: thin full-width header with serif product name "Spironolactone Atlas" on left and readable chapter links "Overview", "Evidence", "Reports", "Sources" on right. Below, a generous dark ink hero split by a precise vertical baseline: left narrative column about 43% width, right quantitative composition about 57% width. Bottom of hero carries small source annotations. Lower quarter of image begins a clearly ordered evidence reading section with title and three numbered reading stations.
Hero left: small monospaced kicker "AN EDUCATIONAL EVIDENCE ATLAS"; clinical elegant serif headline "Data has limits. Understanding starts here." with deliberate line breaks and calm generous leading. Small clear body copy "A source-led study of spironolactone, research evidence and adverse-event reporting." Prominent light filled primary action "Read the story" with small arrow, and understated legible secondary action "Explore data". Visible chapter marker "01 / THE REPORTING PICTURE".
Hero right: one immense clean tabular "52.2%" focal point in warm off-white, accompanied by readable label "No informative indication". Beneath it, a precise two-part rectangular area chart of equal height: coral region occupies exactly 52.2% of width and teal region 47.8%. Label each region legibly, "52.2% — No informative indication" and "47.8% — At least one informative indication", using line breaks. Huge number remains singular focal point; 47.8% subordinate. Under chart concise annotation "Of 24,805 selected reports". Fine aligned lines and measured planar regions make the underlying grid visible. Shapes carry quantitative meaning. No decorative circles, triangles or random blocks.
Hero source footnote: "Source: openFDA • First receipt 2004–2025 • Retrieved 3 Nov 2026". Clear caveat directly below: "Reporting completeness does not establish off-label prescribing prevalence."
Next section on same dark ink field, separated by precise horizontal rule: elegant serif heading "Read the evidence in context." Ordered horizontal reading stations with aligned baselines, restrained numbers and small top coral/teal rules: "01  Label scope", "02  Research evidence", "03  Reporting data". Small footer-like link "Methods and underlying tables →".
ART DIRECTION: Evidence in Proportion, Bauhaus foundation point-line-plane composition adapted to clinical educational editorial reading. The typographic and proportional layout is rigorous, asymmetric, measured and unusually confident while fully usable. Ink #0B1020 ground, warm off-white #F3F0E8 text, coral #F48F7A and teal #65B8AC measured chart planes only. Crisp flat surfaces, no gradients, no shadows or rounded dashboard cards. Elegant clinical editorial serif product name and headline, readable clean sans body, clean monospaced annotations and large tabular sans figures. Strong hierarchy, plentiful breathing room, source annotations readable. At least 50px page gutters. Commit to these material and layout choices, not a generic SaaS template.
All text sharp and accurately spelled. No commercial claims, no invented clinical facts, no prices, no fake anatomy or pills, no yellow or bright red decoration, no stock photography. This is a competitive unapproved design preview, but do not render approval status or design commentary inside the website.
provenance: Original generated decision-stage comp from PRODUCT.md and challenger-bauhaus; no approved mock or copied source composition.
deviations: Generated landscape 1487×1058 rather than approximate 1440×1080; visible source text and quantitative labels verified.
